string-array.name: termux_appearance_color_descriptions
string-array.item: Default text color: what you type and most program output.
Terminal background, behind the text. With a wallpaper on, the wallpaper shows instead wherever this color would be.
The blinking block or bar that shows where you are typing.
Normal black. Used by programs for dark text and shadows, and as a background for status bars.
Errors and failures, deleted lines in diffs, and archives in ls.
Success and OK messages, added lines in diffs, and executable files in ls.
Directories in ls, links and informational text. Often the hardest color to read on dark themes.
Special files, keywords in code editors and prompt decorations.
Symbolic links in ls, strings in code and informational text.
Normal light gray text. Many programs use this instead of the default text color.
Dark gray: comments in code, hints, and dimmed or disabled text.
Brighter red: bold or emphasized errors.
Brighter green: bold or emphasized success, and bold executables.
Brighter yellow: bold warnings and strong highlights.
Brighter blue: bold directories in ls and bold links.
Brighter magenta: bold special files and emphasized keywords.
Brighter cyan: bold symbolic links and emphasized strings.
Pure white: bold text and emphasized output.
